text:
rachel: Noticing a steady stream of SCIM deprovisioning retries from our JP IdP starting ~03:20Z. They look like repeated DELETE /scim/Users for same externalId and creating a deprov-loop. Opening thread.

omar: seeing it too. Logs show 409/200 flipflop: our proxy returns 200 then backend user-service responds 409 duplicate-deprov? weird.

deploy-bot: deploy: sso-proxy v3.5.0 by nina at 2025-01-07T03:15:10Z :rocket:

rachel: suspect cache invalidation: we added a short-lived in-memory session cache in v3.5.0 to reduce KMS decrypt calls. If cache returns stale sessions, webhook auth may fail and trigger deprov fallback.

kevin: can you paste a few lines from the provisioning log?

rachel: sure:

```
2025-01-07T03:22:01Z req=a1 scim_req=del-111 DELETE /scim/Users?externalId=ext-700 status=200 auth_method=session
2025-01-07T03:22:02Z usersvc: lookup externalId=ext-700 -> not found, enqueued backfill-deprov
2025-01-07T03:22:03Z req=a1 scim_req=del-112 DELETE /scim/Users?externalId=ext-700 status=200 auth_method=session
2025-01-07T03:22:04Z usersvc: lookup externalId=ext-700 -> not found, enqueued backfill-deprov
```

omar: looks like session auth succeeded but user service query returns not found; backfill then creates phantom operations. Why auth success if cache stale? maybe cached session maps to tenant A but request is for tenant B due to missing tenant header.

nina: we shipped a tenant-canonicalization change to headers in the same deploy (X-Tenant-Id normalization). Could be interaction: cache keyed by raw tenant header previously, now normalized; some proxies still using older key.

kevin: also found these errors in proxy around same time: `KMSDecrypt: context-mismatch` which suggests our cache stored decrypted tokens with the old KMS context. If cache wasn't invalidated on rotate, tokens could be considered valid but map wrong.

sec-oncall: impact? any user data exposed or RBAC gaps?

rachel: initial triage: ~120 deprov retries for 8 tenants, 23 duplicate audit rows with null correlation_id. No auth bypass observed; flows used session auth only. RBAC enforcement still applied, but audit linkage missing in some backfill paths.

omar: quick mitigation: disable in-memory session cache and revert header normalization for canary clusters. I'll open revert PR.

nina: rolling revert to canary now. ETA 03:45Z.

deploy-bot: revert started: sso-proxy v3.5.0 -> v3.4.9 at 2025-01-07T03:30:12Z

kevin: long-term fixes: 1) ensure cache keys include KMS crypto-context and tenant canonical id, 2) on KMS rotate, flush caches before marking rotation complete, 3) add audit emission in unauthenticated backfill code path so events are recorded.

sec-oncall: create SEC-7601 for postmortem and remediation. Set owner: nina. Add priority: high.

rachel: also recommend we implement HMAC-signed SCIM requests from IdPs to avoid relying on session cookies for webhook auth. Compliance likes it too.

omar: agree. For now, disable backfill auto-create flag while we dedupe. Add metric scim_deprov_retry_rate and alert if >0.05 for >10m.

nina: DB reconcile: I'll run a script to merge duplicate audit entries and map backfill ops to original externalId for the 03:20-03:40 window. Will coordinate downtime window.

kevin: note for KMS team: add a pre-rotate canary that verifies cache flush across all proxy instances and that idp-config refetch works. Also add IAM check for whoever runs rotations (infra:rotate must include s3:PutObject).

sec-oncall: good. I'll schedule a brief postmortem sync in 2h. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
